description: Plays one MPX part on a modelled violin, or on several where notes sound together: four strings bowed through a model of rosin's friction, on one bridge and one body, each note's bowing chosen by a model of a player.

params.name: Vibrato
params.text: How wide the vibrato is, as a share of each note's own width: at the middle, each note's own — wider on long and loud notes, none on open strings or where the part says senza vibrato, narrower in earlier music; at the bottom, none; at the top, twice as wide. A change is heard at once, on the notes already sounding.

inputs.name: MPX note
inputs.text: One part, played on the violin: its notes, from mpxScore or any MPX source. From a score each note is announced ahead, and at Fidelity levels 1 to 3 its start is worked out before it sounds.

inputs.name: Gate
inputs.text: Plays the violin without a cable: a note while the gate is up, let go when it falls. Each channel is a violin of its own, up to sixteen, and the same channel of V/OCT, LEVEL and VIB is that violin's; a one-channel cable into one of those is read by every violin. Each note is played as it comes, as Fidelity's live level plays it, since nothing says ahead what is coming. While an MPX cable is in, this port and the three below it are not read.

inputs.name: 1V/oct
inputs.text: The pitch of the gate's note, a volt an octave, nought at middle C, a channel for each violin. A move of more than half a semitone while the gate stays up is the next note, slurred in the same bow; a smaller one is left alone.

inputs.name: Level
inputs.text: How loud each gate's note is played, read as it begins, a channel for each violin: nought volts ppp, ten fff, in sevenths between. With nothing patched, mf.

inputs.name: Vibrato CV
inputs.text: Added to the VIBRATO knob, a channel for each violin: five volts add as much as the knob's middle, and the sum is held between none and twice each note's own width.

outputs.name: Out
outputs.text: The violins playing, summed, in mono. Each is as loud as mpxPiano playing the same markings: a single note at fff peaks about 2.5V.

lights.name: Level
lights.text: Flashes green as each note begins, lights orange when the output passes 7.07V, 3 dB under clipping, and red when it reaches 10V, where Rack's audio interface clips.

notes: From a score, each note is announced to the module three seconds before it sounds. At Fidelity levels 1 to 3, ways of starting it are tried on a copy of the violin while the music plays. A note from a keyboard or a generator, which nothing announced, is played as it arrives.

Notes sounding together, a chord on the cable or the channels of a polyphonic gate, are each played by a violin of its own, up to sixteen. From the cable, the highest note of a chord goes to the first violin, the next to the second, and so on; a note that starts as another ends goes to the violin that played that one, so a line stays on one violin. The first violin is in tune; the others are tuned up to four cents sharp or flat, and their vibratos run at slightly different rates. Each violin playing takes as much computing as a module of its own; one with nothing to play takes almost none.

Fidelity, in the right-click menu, sets how much is tried on a copy of the violin before each note sounds. Level 1 tries up to eighteen ways of starting each note from the string, and each bow change three ways. Level 2 tries two ways of starting, a short glide and one bite. Level 3 plays one bite without trying it and still tries each bow change. Level 4, the default, tries nothing: each note is played as it arrives, so notes need not be announced ahead, and no second copy of the violin is worked out, for the least computing.

Economy, in the right-click menu, is for less computing at less fidelity: the strings are worked out at half the rate, and a string nobody is playing stops once it has rung down, so it no longer rings in sympathy with the others. It takes about half the computing.
